page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-48 is a general-purpose server instance powered by an Intel x86_64 processor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs derived from 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2.0 threads per core. The instance is configured with 192 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU architecture includes a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512).

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and specialized execution capabilities. The server achieves a PassMark CPU score of 58,480.28 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17,663.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Large-block memory bandwidth is also strong, with read speeds of 259.28 GB/sec and write speeds of 114.19 GB/sec. In contrast, single-core performance remains in the average range, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1,869.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1,783.48. The hardware acceleration for vector and matrix operations is reflected in strong scores for PassMark extended instructions and encryption.

A notable architectural tradeoff is the complete absence of local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, meaning all storage requirements must be met via network-attached options. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-48 offers high resource density for multi-threaded workloads, leveraging its dedicated physical cores and large L3 cache to deliver strong database operations and static web serving throughput without the premium cost of specialized memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware.

This server configuration is suitable for multi-threaded enterprise applications, database operations, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning tasks. The presence of Intel AMX instructions enables strong prompt processing speeds for small and medium LLM models, making it a viable option for intermediate AI inference workloads that do not require dedicated GPU hardware.

It lacks local storage and complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network storage. Single-core performance is average, but the inclusion of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions drives strong results in cryptography, database operations, and small-to-medium LLM prompt processing. This configuration is highly efficient for multi-threaded workloads, database servers, static web serving, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
